properties.details_shown: Fog, tar, and gulls; the far piers are rotting. Pier four has an upturned skiff where Sela mends a net.

sources.quote: Morning in Gullwick. The fog is still sitting on the docks, gulls everywhere, and you're standing at the end of pier four looking for a boat.
There's a woman sitting on an upturned skiff, mending a net. Grey braid, salt-stained coat. She doesn't look up.

changes.why: Adds the dock details shown this session.

properties.role: Tide-reader and boatwoman at Gullwick Docks.
properties.played_as: Whispers as if the water might hear her; avoids eye contact, watches the tide line, and returns to mending her net. Grey braid and salt-stained coat.
properties.wants: Will row the party to the old chapel by day, never at night; says she will wait at pier four tomorrow at first light.
properties.knows: Says Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang, forty years ago; her grandmother said the water rose warm.

sources.quote: Sela Thorn. I read the tides. I'll row you, but not at night. Never at night.
There's a woman sitting on an upturned skiff, mending a net. Grey braid, salt-stained coat. She doesn't look up.
She talks in a whisper, like the water might hear her, and she never once looks you in the eye. She keeps her gaze on the tide line.
Sela, Sella, the dockhands say it both ways.
Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.
She shrugs and goes back to her net. She says she'll be at pier four tomorrow at first light if you want the ride.

changes.why: Records the newly voiced NPC, her aliases, manner, offer, and attributed knowledge.

sources.quote: She shrugs and goes back to her net. She says she'll be at pier four tomorrow at first light if you want the ride.

changes.why: Sela was last seen at pier four.

properties.statement: Sela says Saltmere flooded forty years ago on the night the bell first rang; according to her grandmother, the rising water was warm.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: Preserves Sela's account and its secondhand detail without establishing the historical claim as confirmed.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: Identifies the mine in Sela's account.

change.name: Saltmere's flooding and the first bell

properties.what_is_open: Was Saltmere's flooding connected to the first ringing of the bell, as Sela claims?

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: Sela's claim raises an unresolved connection between the mine and the bell.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: Records who supplied this lead.

properties.details_shown: Up the cliff path, closed for forty years. A black entrance in chalk with a half-rotted timber frame and an overturned rusted cart. Warm air smells of old candle wax. Thirty paces in, warm black water floods the tunnel, with wet hymn-book pages floating and stuck to the walls.
properties.state: Closed; the tunnel is flooded about thirty paces inside.

sources.quote: The Saltmere Mine entrance is a black mouth in the chalk, timber frame half rotted. A rusted cart lies on its side. The air coming out of it is warm and smells like a church, like old candle wax.
About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch. Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.

changes.why: Records the mine's observed condition and descriptions.

change.name: The hymn page marked M. Brand

properties.statement: A hymn-book page found in Saltmere's warm flooded tunnel describes the sea giving back what it takes and has "M. Brand" penciled in its margin.

sources.quote: About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch. Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.
A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".

changes.why: Records the clue without confirming who wrote it or where the book originated.

sources.quote: About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch. Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.
A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".

changes.why: Records where the hymn clue was found.

properties.role: Teo Brand's sister, sought after leaving the Archive.

sources.quote: That's Mira. That's my sister's handwriting. She was here.

changes.why: Adds the named sister already established in Teo's existing goal; her handwriting and presence at the mine remain Teo's inference.

properties.what_changed: Mira heard the bell the night she left. At Saltmere, a hymn page bears "M. Brand"; Teo believes the handwriting is Mira's and infers she was there.

sources.quote: A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".
That's Mira. That's my sister's handwriting. She was here.

changes.why: Advances Teo's goal with the observed clue and his explicitly attributed identification.

properties.what_is_open: Vessa suspects Maren is behind the events and belongs to a cult; Oren suspects she runs the Choir. Neither claim is confirmed.

sources.quote: Okay, I bet the harbor-master is behind all this. Maren wanted us gone from day one. She's in the cult, I'm calling it.
Yeah, Maren is totally running the choir.
You can think that. Roll investigation if you want to search the rest.

changes.why: Keeps the players' theory in a thread rather than changing Maren's established state.

properties.details_shown: Previously described as having sunk into the bay with its bell. At low water, the bell tower and two broken arches protrude from the bay; seaweed hangs from the stones. At midnight, pale shapes stand in rows on the submerged chapel floor like a congregation, then vanish when the bell stops.

sources.quote: The drowned chapel's roof sticks out of the bay at low water, just the bell tower and two broken arches. Seaweed hangs from the stones.
Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation. Then the bell stops and they're gone.

changes.why: Adds the chapel's visible ruins and the temporary shapes without assigning them identities.

properties.statement: Local fishermen say the Kelp Mother pulls children who stand too close to the water down by their ankles; her existence is unconfirmed.

sources.quote: Don't stand that close. The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.
That's what the fishermen say. They pull their boat up and leave.

changes.why: Records the fishermen's warning as a rumor, not an NPC or a confirmed creature.

sources.quote: That's the choir clock at three of six.

changes.why: Applies the GM's explicit story-clock advancement from two to three of six.

properties.what_is_open: Who or what rings the submerged bell? It rang twelve times again at midnight; the humming was much louder, and pale shapes stood in rows on the chapel floor before vanishing when the bell stopped.

sources.quote: And then, right at midnight, the bell rings again under the water. Twelve times. And the humming is back, but louder. Much louder than two nights ago. You can feel it in your teeth.
Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation. Then the bell stops and they're gone.

changes.why: Advances the existing bell mystery with directly observed escalation.

properties.details_shown: A tavern by Gullwick Docks, with a fire burning and smells of tar and fish stew.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.

changes.why: Records the named tavern and the GM's description.

properties.played_as: Huge, with a red beard; laughs at his own jokes and wipes the same mug throughout the conversation. Teases the party as brave or stupid and gives them stew on the house.
properties.knows: Says he has known Maren for thirty years, calls her sharp-tongued and good-hearted, and says she lost a brother to the bay.

sources.quote: The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.
You lot went to the shore at midnight? Brave or stupid. On the house, either way.
Bram is huge, red beard, laughs at his own jokes, and he wipes the same mug the whole time he talks to you.
Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: Records the newly voiced innkeeper, his manner, and his attributed account of Maren.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.
The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.

changes.why: Bram works at the Tarred Gull.

sources.quote: The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.

changes.why: Records where the party last saw Bram.

change.name: Bram's account of Maren's lost brother

properties.statement: Bram says he has known Maren for thirty years and that she lost a brother to the bay; he describes her as sharp-tongued and good-hearted.

sources.quote: Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: Preserves Bram's testimony without turning his character judgment or family account into narration.

sources.quote: Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

properties.next_step: The party plans for Sela to row them out tomorrow at first light, then to dive to the chapel at low tide in daylight.

sources.quote: At low tide, during the day. Not at night, Sela was right about that.
So tomorrow, first light, Sela rows us out and we dive to the chapel at low tide. I'll buy rope and a second lantern tonight.
Agreed. Tomorrow we dive.

changes.why: Records the agreed next step as an intention, not an accomplished dive or a story deadline.

properties.what_changed: Mira heard the bell the night she left. A Saltmere hymn page bears "M. Brand", which Teo identifies as Mira's handwriting. He believes the hymns came from the chapel; the party plans to dive there tomorrow in daylight at low tide.

sources.quote: Okay, plan. Mira wrote in that hymn book. The chapel is where the hymns came from. We go down to the chapel.
So tomorrow, first light, Sela rows us out and we dive to the chapel at low tide. I'll buy rope and a second lantern tonight.

changes.why: Carries Teo's unconfirmed interpretation and the agreed dive plan forward in his goal.
